newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt up on expectations of no Fed action.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt up on expectations of no Fed action.

text.p: Brady bond prices were mostly higher on Wednesday on expectations the U.S. Federal Reserve would keep interest rates steady, emerging market traders said.

"I don't think anyone is expecting the Fed to move. They will look at the (U.S.) jobs data but...the trend recently has been for reasonably sedate data so if that continues we will continue to see the bond trade up," said one Brady bond trader at a European bank in London.
At around 1800 GMT, the Fed will announce results of its Federal Open Market Committee meeting but a Reuters poll of U.S. analysts unanimously forecast no change in U.S. monetary policy.
Meanwhile, high yielding instruments, such as Bulgaria and Ecuador, benefitted the most from bond friendly figures released on Tuesday and market experts said that trend should continue.
The National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) report triggered a sharp runup in U.S. Treasury securities, thus spurring a similar rise in the Brady market.
Among the Latin American credits, Ecuadorean PDIs ECPDI=RR extended its 1-1/2 point gain from New York's closing levels rising 1/2 to 66-1/2 bid.

As for Eastern European debt instruments, Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR firmed an additional 5/8 to 73-3/4 bid a day after the implementation of a currency board system, which pegs the lev to the mark. Scattered demand from investors also helped to push Russian loans marginally higher, with Vneshekonombank dollar-denominated debt RUVNUSLNS=RR rising 1/2 to 92-1/2 bid.

Although a flurry of activity is expected following the release of the June U.S. employment report on Thursday, emerging market experts said Friday should remain extremely thin because of the U.S. Independance Day Holiday.
"London will be a full day tomorrow but people will be in only a half day on Friday" because of the July 4th holiday, a trader said.
